Theorem
[Interior Hessian estimate under natural structure] 1. ch17:17.15\group chapter-17Source: gilbarg-trudinger:page-0474 Let $u\in C^4(\Omega )$ solve $F[u]=0$ in $\Omega \subset \mathbb R^n$. Suppose $F$ is concave or convex jointly in $z,p,r$ and satisfies (17.53). Then \begin{equation} \tag {17.54} |u|^*_{2,\alpha ;\Omega }\le C, \end{equation} where $\alpha >0$ depends only on $n$ and $\Lambda (M)/\lambda (M)$, and $C$ also depends on $\mu (M)$, $\operatorname {diam}\Omega $, and $M=|u|_{0;\Omega }$.
Proof

\sketch Joint concavity removes the $F_{rp},F_{rz},F_{pp},F_{pz},F_{zz}$ terms from the differentiated inequality. Conditions (17.53) and Theorem 17.14 give $|u|^*_{2,\alpha }\le C(1+|u|^*_2)$; interior interpolation absorbs $|u|^*_2$ into the zeroth-order bound.

□
